story.title: Fujitsu launches made-in-Japan next-generation CPU FUJITSU-MONAKA

draft:
Japan just put a new CPU on the world stage.

Fujitsu’s “MONAKA” is the first high‑performance processor designed and fabricated entirely in Japan. It promises a tighter supply chain, lower latency for domestic AI workloads, and a design that prioritises security‑by‑hardware—something we’ve been lacking in a market dominated by overseas fabs.

What catches my eye is the timing. As global chip shortages ease, a home‑grown silicon strategy could give Japanese firms a competitive edge in edge‑AI and autonomous systems, while also reducing geopolitical risk. If the architecture lives up to its specs, we might see a shift in how multinational cloud providers source their compute.

I’m curious: will other regions follow suit and build sovereign processors, or will they double‑down on existing ecosystems?
